title: Box Out and Hold Two Seconds
description: Partners practise the box-out technique on a shot, holding the position for a full two seconds before releasing to go get the ball.

content.objective: Find and hold a legal box-out position long enough for a shot to actually come down.
content.setup: Partners stand near the block, one as the shooter's defender boxing out the other.
instructions: On the shot, the defender pivots and makes contact with a wide base, back to the offensive player.
Hold the position with arms up for a full two-second count.
Release and go get the rebound once the two seconds are up.
Switch roles after five reps each.
coachingPoints: Make contact with the back and hips, not by reaching with the arms.
Keep a wide, low base to hold the position.
Go get the ball — boxing out alone doesn't finish the job.
commonMistakes: Releasing the box-out too early to chase the ball.
Reaching with the arms instead of using the lower body for contact.
Reaching for the ball with one hand instead of securing it with two.
content.safety: Make contact with the body only, no grabbing or holding the opponent's jersey.
